### Heliograph messages (session start)

Only when `command -v helio` (or `Get-Command helio -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` in PowerShell) succeeds and `helio.conf` is found in the repository or a folder above it, run `helio hello antigravity` once per session on initial `process-phase` entry (whether started directly or as the first phase of `process-plan`; skip on subsequent phases of the same session):

```sh
if command -v helio >/dev/null 2>&1 && { d=$PWD; while [ "$d" != "/" ]; do [ -f "$d/helio.conf" ] && break; p=$(dirname "$d"); [ "$p" = "$d" ] && break; d=$p; done; [ -f "$d/helio.conf" ]; }; then helio hello antigravity; fi
```

```powershell
if ((Get-Command helio -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (& { $d = (Get-Location).Path; while ($d) { if (Test-Path (Join-Path $d 'helio.conf')) { return $true }; $p = Split-Path $d -Parent; if ($p -eq $d) { break }; $d = $p }; return $false })) { helio hello antigravity }
```

On resume, only after the run guard confirms this session is the sole writer (preventing overlapping recovery runs), scan the prior run file in chronological order and reconcile every ID whose latest Critical events entry is `helio-claim: <id>` or `release-pending` (never letting an earlier `error` entry suppress a newer `helio-claim: <id>`): first scan `todo/` for `Heliograph: <id>`; if a section already carries `Heliograph: <id>`, never release it or file a duplicate, and persist `helio-ref: <id> -> <existing ref>`; otherwise never file a TODO from an unverified claim, and first run `helio show <id>` to inspect who holds it: if `helio show <id>` exits 2 or 3 keep `release-pending` for retry at the next boundary, if `<id>` is open, closed, or `taken by` another lane never call `release` and record `not-held`, and only when `<id>` is `taken by` this lane run `helio release <id>` (recording `released` only on exit 0, or keeping `release-pending` on exit 2 or 3 for retry at the next boundary). Exit 1 is normal; exit 2 or 3 writes a single sanitized diagnostic (exit code and non-secret error summary, never raw message text) once under Critical events and the run carries on.

Before deciding or filing any ID, scan `todo/` for `Heliograph: <id>` (so a job already filed before a crash or in another phase is never filed twice and only repairs `helio-ref: <id> -> <existing ref>`). For an in-scope request, write `helio-claim: <id>` under Critical events before calling `helio take <id>` (lane-scoped without `--session`), then file through `add-todo` only when `helio take <id>` exits 0 (a refused claim never files a TODO and closes the intent as `error (exit <N>)`); record `Heliograph: <id>` in the filed TODO section body (so whichever phase ships it closes the job) and `helio-ref: <id> -> DNN TNN §N` in the run file, reading that mapping back on later polls so an already-taken job is not filed twice; if filing cannot proceed after a successful `take`, run `helio release <id>` and record `released` only when it exits 0 (recording `release-pending` on exit 2 or 3 for retry at the next boundary so the claim is never stranded). Leave any out-of-scope request open for its owner. Because the run file is committed and pushed, record only the message ID and local disposition (`skipped`, `taken -> DNN TNN §N`, `released`, `not-held`, `release-pending`, `done`, `done-pending`, or sanitized `error (exit <N>)`) under Critical events, never raw message bodies, session identifiers, or private inbox text. Heliograph never stops, parks, pauses or ends a run: exit 1 (nothing new) is normal; exit 2 (refused) or exit 3 (damaged store) writes a single sanitized diagnostic (exit code and non-secret error summary, no message body) once in the run file and the run carries on to the next row (on exit 3 with partial inbox output, still inspect any IDs printed before damage and then carry on).
